obligations.question: Define one concrete three-or-more-phase Bombay actor protocol and justify its relevance.
obligations.decision: Supervised Worker Lifecycle: Starting -> Running -> Draining, with direction-sensitive messages (Configure IN from supervisor, Work IN from clients, Result OUT to clients). Actor-relevant because it exercises supervision linkage, peer watching, child creation, and drain coordination — all actor-specific concerns beyond generic channel protocols.

obligations.question: Specify valid traces, phase-local messages, transitions, termination, initialization, and errors.
obligations.decision: Valid trace: Start -> Configure -> Running -> Work* -> DrainStatus -> Draining -> DrainStatus* -> Stop(Normal). Per-phase messages: InitEvent{Configure}, RunningEvent{Work,Drain}, DrainingEvent{DrainStatus}. Invalid transitions: Work in Starting, Configure in Running, Work in Draining. Termination via DrainStatus when in-flight queue is empty. Init is a no-op (no initial sends). Errors: Never (FSM transition function is infallible for this protocol).

obligations.question: List the exact invalid programs that must fail to compile and why runtime rejection is insufficient.
obligations.decision: Four invalid programs: (1) Work event for Starting-phase behavior, (2) Configure event for Running-phase behavior, (3) Work event for Draining-phase behavior, (4) Result (outbound) where Work (inbound) expected. Runtime rejection (FSM deferral) is insufficient because it defers rather than rejects — the message is held and replayed after phase change, which may be semantically wrong (e.g., stale configuration after the worker has already started).

obligations.question: Separate actor-model laws, session-type results, Bombay derivations, policies, and application choices using primary sources.
obligations.decision: LAW: per-actor serialization (Agha 1986 §3.1.1), acquaintance addressing (Agha 1986 §3.2.1), become (Agha 1986 §3.1.3). SESSION-TYPE (not actor-model law): Honda-style duality requires both endpoints known at compile time (Honda CONCUR'93, ESOP'98) — incompatible with dynamic acquaintance. BOMBAY-DERIVED: Fsm from receive+become, Behavior::Event as single associated type. BOMBAY-POLICY: compile-time phase safety not a design goal of current algebra; Ph tracks values not types.

obligations.question: Test the concrete case against current Fsm and state precisely what it can and cannot guarantee.
obligations.decision: FSM CAN: correctly sequence phases at runtime (Starting->Running->Draining->Stop), defer invalid-phase messages for later replay, drain deferred messages on phase change, never drop or duplicate messages (proven by existing proptest suites). FSM CANNOT: prevent construction of invalid-phase events at compile time, distinguish inbound from outbound messages at the type level, encode a transition relation that excludes invalid phase transitions.

obligations.question: Attempt a public-API derivation using Behavior, associated types, sums, products, typestate, and uninhabited types.
obligations.decision: Attempted phase-indexed typestate: WorkerBehavior<InitPhase> with Event=InitEvent, WorkerBehavior<RunningPhase> with Event=RunningEvent. Obstruction: Behavior::Event is a single associated type — each phase would be a different concrete type, but the driver holds &mut B for a single B. Step::Goto(Ph) transitions by value, not by type; uninhabited phase markers have no Goto values; inhabited markers lose type discrimination. No reusable public-API derivation succeeded.

obligations.question: Attempt an application-local concrete behavior before proposing reusable core API.
obligations.decision: WorkerApp enum with Starting/Running/Draining variants, AppMsg flat enum, manual dispatch via if let on phase variant. Distinguished per-phase event types (InitEvent, RunningEvent) are type-distinct but cannot be used with the Behavior trait's single Event type.

obligations.question: Record exact compiler/type/composition obstruction for every failed derivation.
obligations.decision: Five obstructions: (1) Fixed Event type — Behavior::Event is a single associated type, cannot vary by phase. (2) No runtime type change — driver holds &mut B for single B; phase transition would change B's concrete type. (3) Ph is value index not type index — Step::Goto(Ph) carries runtime value, does not constrain Event. (4) Actor addressing precludes session duality — dynamic acquaintance vs static duality. (5) Wrapper composition — every wrapper depends on single Event type; phase-varying Event would break all wrappers.

obligations.question: Check Actions preservation and relevant wrapper orders, initialization, errors, termination, and births.
obligations.decision: FSM composes with all wrappers: Fsm implements Behavior with single Event=User<A,M>, Ph=Never, Birth=NoBirths, Sends=Vec<Delivery<A,Never>>. All wrappers (Watching, Supervising, At, ReceiveTimeout, Stashing, Shutdown) compose over this signature unconditionally. A phase-varying Event would require each wrapper to be generic over the phase type AND to propagate phase transitions — breaking the universal composition contract. Test confirms FSM composes with Watching.

obligations.question: Actively try to falsify the preferred outcome with a competing derivation and adversarial examples.
obligations.decision: Competing derivation: use existing UserEvent extraction traits for phase-filtered message routing. This works at runtime (extraction traits return Option<Self>) but does not make invalid-phase events unrepresentable — it's still a runtime check. Adversarial example: WorkerMsg::Work sent to Starting-phase FSM compiles, runs, is deferred — not rejected. Session-type duality: fundamentally incompatible with actor acquaintance addressing (dynamic discovery vs static duality).

obligations.question: Choose exactly one allowed outcome and explain why the other outcomes were rejected.
obligations.decision: Outcome: application-local. The existing FSM handles runtime phase sequencing correctly. Applications CAN build per-phase event types (InitEvent, RunningEvent) but cannot bridge them to the Behavior trait's single Event type. No reusable core construction is lawful because: (1) changing Behavior::Event to vary by phase would break every wrapper, (2) dynamic dispatch is prohibited, (3) the obstruction is in the trait contract, not a missing primitive. Rejected existing-algebra-sufficient because per-phase event types are possible but not integrated; rejected minimal-core-gap because no concrete derivation failure proved an algebraic gap requiring a new primitive; rejected insufficient-evidence because the evidence is concrete and complete.
